judgements.justification: Both area chairs followed their reviewers' scores; neither set the recommendation from their own reading.
Neither committee's recommendation rests on a forecast of impact beyond the paper's setting.
A's main critic oMsG raised his score to 6 after the response; in B the near-identical framing and human-study explanation moved no score.
A's spotlight rests on wEz8's 9 at confidence 5, a two-hour review that is mostly summary with three minor points and never addresses the sample selection.
Only B raised unreported inference speed (jmVT) and unmeasured parser errors (2tE8), and B's meta-review cites both against the paper.
Both committees saw the hand-designed world model, thin novelty and stretched System 1/2 framing; A took them as stated limits of a proof of concept, B as fatal to generality.
No score moved from reviewer discussion; oMsG's rise followed the authors' response.
Each rating matches its review's verdict; CnYk's 4 sits with a review that names applicability, novelty and openness concerns.
Confidences are 4 or 5 throughout; no reviewer said they could not judge the paper.
A's meta-review cites consensus and the mean, not wEz8's verdict; B's chair summarised all four reviews.
B's reviewers did not write accept-like verdicts at low scores; they judged the world model too limiting, a different verdict, not a different calibration.
A's meta-review cites unanimity, but wEz8 rated 9, above the accept level, so the reason's condition fails.
oMsG raised his score on reframing, arguments and promised citations and wording fixes; no new result was shown.
A's four-sentence meta-review names no weakness, dropping oMsG's novelty, evaluation and citation points, while B's meta-review carries every reviewer's concern forward.
B's two lowest scores rest partly on wrong claims: Ms3t (3) on gSCAN validity and missing baselines, CnYk (4) on a supervised-trained parser.
The concession that the world model must be designed per domain went to B, which already rejected; A received no damaging concession about results.
CnYk's post-response grounds (closed GPT-3, novelty) were already in the original review, and the authors had answered them.
The committees' scores are far apart (mean 7.0 against 4.25), not near-identical.
No area chair passed over a better-informed reviewer; B's reviewers are all at confidence 4 and A's chair followed all four.
A's critic raised framing, citation and evaluation-design points the response could clarify; B's decisive concern, the hand-built world model, is scope the response could only concede.
wEz8's 9 lifts A from poster to spotlight territory, but A's other scores (6, 6, 7) still sit well above B's (5, 4, 3, 5).
wEz8, the flagged outlier, never engaged, but the response answered no point its 9 rested on; Ms3t ignored the response but is not an outlier in B.
Neither committee had a discarded detractor.
No reviewer raised audience breadth or venue fit.
Neither meta-review misstates the reviewers' final positions or the response; B's omits the corrected misreadings but does not rest on them.
B's reviewers mostly replied to the response and kept their scores; A's non-engaging reviewers held scores whose basis the response did not answer.
All reviewers are at confidence 4 or 5 and none said they could not verify the results.
Neither committee was split evenly.
The authors gave both committees the same account of the framing and the human study; the world-model limitation is stated in the paper itself.
Novelty criticism in both committees cites relevant prior work correctly; no wrong precedent or accepted false first claim.
A's meta-review gives no reason for a spotlight over a poster, and only wEz8's thin 9 supports that tier.
The framing objections (System 1/2) came from both committees and were not argued from a neighbouring field's premises.
A's only high-scoring reviewer, wEz8, gave a light review and never engaged, so A had no engaged champion either.
No committee rejected because promised revisions were too large.
No off-record input appears in either committee's record.

reasoning: The core of the split is the same facts weighted differently: A took the hand-built world model, thin novelty and stretched framing as stated limits of a proof of concept, B as fatal to generality (R06, R20). The rebuttal moved A's critic on explanations and promises but no B score (R03, R13). A's spotlight rests on one thin 9 and a meta-review that names no weakness and gives no reason for the tier (R04, R14, R31). B's lowest scores rest partly on misreadings (R15), and B alone raised inference speed and parser errors (R05). The stage 1 candidates all map to existing reasons: CnYk's closed-GPT-3 ground was in the original review, so no late-objection or shifted-ground reason is needed. R21 fails because A's other scores stay well above B's. No new reason was added.
